findings.title: Shift scheduling is entirely unbuilt — the Shifts tab is permanently read-only
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/api/shifts/shifts.ts (Orval-generated) only exports useShiftControllerGetAll and useShiftControllerGetOne — no create/update/delete hook exists. A repo-wide search found zero routes or components calling any shift-mutation hook. There is no screen anywhere in the app where a manager can create, edit, or remove a staff shift.
findings.recommendation: Add POST/PATCH/DELETE shift endpoints with full Swagger decorators, regenerate the Orval client, and add at least a slot-tap → create-shift flow (or a dedicated staff-scheduling screen) before this tab ships — right now half of this screen's stated purpose is unreachable.

findings.title: Overlapping bookings render as illegible slivers with mid-word text wrapping
findings.evidence: Tablet screenshot, Friday evening: two simultaneous reservations ('9:30 PM Julia & ...' and '10:00 ... Th...') are laid out as two narrow side-by-side columns with clipped, unreadable labels. The single 2:30 PM 'Becker' event above it wraps mid-word into 'Becke' / 'r' on two lines inside its own block. No truncation-with-ellipsis, tooltip, or '+N more' affordance is used.
findings.recommendation: Cap event block text to a single truncated line (ellipsis + native title tooltip, or a details popover on tap) and use react-big-calendar's built-in event limit / 'show more' for overlapping slots instead of letting the library's default overlap layout squeeze text into unreadable columns.

findings.title: No event or slot interactivity — the calendar is display-only
findings.evidence: The <Calendar> element in apps/web/src/routes/_app/calendar/index.tsx only sets localizer, events, defaultView, views, date, onNavigate, scrollToTime, style, and eventPropGetter — no onSelectEvent, onSelectSlot, or selectable prop. Tapping a reservation block or an empty time slot does nothing.
findings.recommendation: Wire onSelectEvent to open a detail view (party size, phone, notes for reservations; staff/role/time for shifts) and, where the create flow lives elsewhere (reservations are created on /door), at minimum deep-link a tapped reservation event to its /door record so the calendar isn't a dead end.

findings.title: 'N reservations this week' is computed from the entire reservations table, not the visible week
findings.evidence: useReservationControllerGetAll() is called with no arguments even though ReservationControllerGetAllParams supports from/to filtering (confirmed in apps/web/src/api/reservations/reservations.ts) — exactly the pattern used correctly for shifts (useShiftControllerGetAll({ from, to })). eventCount = reservationEvents.length therefore reflects every reservation ever created, mislabeled as 'this week,' and won't change when the user pages Back/Next to a different week.
findings.recommendation: Pass { from, to } into useReservationControllerGetAll the same way shifts already do, and derive the header count from events actually falling inside the current week range.

findings.title: Week grid doesn't adapt to phone width — all 7 columns survive, crushed and illegible
findings.evidence: Phone screenshot (780px logical): day headers truncate to '05 St', '06 M', '07 Tu', '08 W', '09 Tl', and event labels shrink to 2-3 characters ('2:30 Be ck', '8:00 Na'). No day-view fallback or horizontal-scroll-per-day is used at this breakpoint — the same fixed 7-column week grid from tablet is just squeezed.
findings.recommendation: Below a width threshold, default to Day view (already available via the Week/Day toggle) or make the week grid horizontally scroll one/two days at a time instead of rendering all 7 columns at a width that can't fit legible text.

findings.title: Toolbar buttons (Today/Back/Next/Week/Day) are under the 44px touch-target minimum
findings.evidence: The toolbar is restyled via arbitrary-value Tailwind selectors targeting react-big-calendar's internal classes: '[&_.rbc-toolbar_button]:px-3 [&_.rbc-toolbar_button]:py-1 [&_.rbc-toolbar_button]:text-sm' — py-1 (4px) + text-sm line-height gives an effective control height well under 44px, and it bypasses the app's normal Button component entirely.
findings.recommendation: Bump vertical padding to at least py-2.5/py-3 (or wrap the toolbar in the shared Button component) so Today/Back/Next/Week/Day meet the same touch-target floor as every other primary control in the app.

findings.title: No Month view
findings.evidence: views={[Views.WEEK, Views.DAY]} — only Week and Day are enabled; there's no way to see a month-at-a-glance reservation/staffing load.
findings.recommendation: Low priority for a waiter/host-first tool, but worth adding a Month view for the manager persona who plans staffing/covers further ahead — react-big-calendar supports it with one more entry in the views array.

findings.title: No loading state while reservations/shifts/staff are fetching
findings.evidence: All three queries destructure with default empty-array fallbacks (data: reservations = [], etc.) and there's no isLoading/skeleton branch, so the subtitle briefly reads '0 reservations this week' and the grid is empty until data arrives.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight skeleton or muted 'Loading…' state for the header count and grid so the empty flash doesn't read as 'no reservations exist.'

perScreen.screenSummary: A clean, on-brand three-section settings page (Restaurant Info, Appearance/theme picker, Notifications) that reflows correctly from tablet to phone and respects the one-primary-CTA rule and semantic-token discipline. It reads as intentional and warm rather than generic. But it is thinner than it looks: the touch targets on every input and button in this dense form are well under the 44px tablet minimum, there's no error state if the profile fails to load, and — most damaging for trust — the Restaurant Info a manager saves here (name/address/phone) is never actually read anywhere else in the app; the printed checkout receipt hardcodes a different restaurant name. The /staff redirect this screen also serves as a landing pad for is an unexplained dead end with no staff-management content anywhere in the product.
positives: Exactly one primary CTA in view: 'Save changes' is the only bg-accent button; the notification Enable/Disable action correctly uses the outline/secondary style.
Responsive reflow is genuinely solid: the 2-column Restaurant Info grid collapses cleanly to a single full-width column at 780px with no cramped or overlapping fields.

Theme selector is well-built: swatch + label + description + accent ring + checkmark gives an unambiguous 'this is currently active' state, and covers 4 themes (default/midnight/monokai/gruvbox) with legible copy.
Visual identity (serif headings, terracotta accent, card/separator rhythm on warm paper) is consistent and reads premium, not templated 'AI slop'.
Good conditional logic: the 'Install App' card only renders when canInstall && !installed, and a blocked notification permission surfaces a clear inline error instead of failing silently.

findings.title: Restaurant Info is saved but never actually used anywhere — receipt hardcodes a different name
findings.evidence: Settings' Restaurant Info card (tablet + phone screenshots) is captioned 'Update your restaurant's public-facing details' and edits Name/Description/Phone/Email/Address (currently 'La Bella Tavola'). But apps/web/src/routes/_app/checkout/-receipt-block.tsx line 8 declares `const RESTAURANT_NAME = 'RestoManager';` and prints that constant on the customer-facing receipt — it never reads useSettingsControllerGet or the saved name/address/phone at all.
findings.recommendation: Wire the printable receipt (and any other customer-facing surface) to read the saved Settings values instead of a hardcoded constant, or relabel the Restaurant Info section so it doesn't over-promise 'public-facing' impact it doesn't have yet.

findings.title: Every interactive control on this form is under the 44px touch-target minimum
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/components/ui/input.tsx sets `h-8` (32px) on all text inputs — all 5 fields in Restaurant Info (Name, Description, Phone, Email, Address) plus Opening Hours use it. button.tsx's default size is also `h-8` (32px, used by 'Save changes') and the `sm` size is `h-7` (28px, used by the Enable/Disable notification toggle). This is the densest form-heavy screen in the app, so the shortfall is most visible here.
findings.recommendation: Bump Input/Button minimum height to ~44px (h-11) at least for default/sm sizes used in form contexts on tablet/phone, or add a touch-optimized size variant used by Settings and other data-entry screens.

findings.title: /staff redirects here silently with zero staff-management content anywhere in the app
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/routes/_app/staff/index.tsx is just `beforeLoad: () => { throw redirect({ to: '/settings' }) }` with no message. The Settings screen (both viewports) has no staff/user/role content, and the sidebar in the screenshots has no Staff nav item at all — so a stale link/bookmark to /staff dead-ends on unrelated Restaurant Info/Appearance/Notifications with no explanation of what happened to staff management.
findings.recommendation: Either delete the vestigial /staff route entirely (if staff management is intentionally gone under the shared-login model) or restore a minimal staff view — a silent, unexplained redirect is worse than a 404.

findings.title: No error state for a failed settings load — a network hiccup renders a blank form with no warning
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/routes/_app/settings/index.tsx line 26: `const { data, isLoading } = useSettingsControllerGet();` — only isLoading is checked (line 113); there's no isError/error branch. If the GET fails, every field silently falls back to '' via the effect at line 80-89, and the manager sees an apparently-empty-but-editable form with no banner explaining why.
findings.recommendation: Add an isError branch with a retry affordance before rendering the form, so a failed load can't be mistaken for 'my restaurant info got wiped' and accidentally overwritten with blanks on Save.

findings.title: Opening Hours is unstructured free text with no day-by-day model
findings.evidence: index.tsx lines 184-194: `<textarea>` bound directly to a single openingHours string (current value 'Mon–Fri 11:00–23:00, Sat–Sun 10:00–23:30'), with a differently-formatted multi-line placeholder example. There's no per-day open/close/closed structure, so nothing else in the app (e.g. an 'open now' indicator) can consume it, and formatting consistency depends entirely on whoever types it.
findings.recommendation: Model opening hours as structured per-day data (even a simple 7-row open/close/closed picker) if anything downstream is meant to read it; otherwise keep it as a clearly-labeled free-text note and don't imply structure via the placeholder.

findings.title: 'Description' is public-facing copy crammed into a single-line input that visibly truncates it
findings.evidence: Both tablet and phone screenshots show the Description field clipped mid-word: 'Modern Italian cuisine with a cozy atmos…' — it's a `<Input type="text">` (line 141-147), not a textarea, so there's no way to review the full saved text without clicking in and scrolling horizontally.
findings.recommendation: Use a small textarea (like Opening Hours) or an expand-to-view affordance for Description so staff can actually read what they saved.

findings.title: Loading state is a bare sentence that discards the page identity
findings.evidence:
Line 113: `if (isLoading) return
Loading…
;` replaces the entire page — including the 'Settings' heading and subtitle — with unstyled muted text, a noticeable step down from the card-based skeletons this design system's polish elsewhere implies.
findings.recommendation: Render the PageHeader plus skeleton cards during load instead of swapping the whole page for a text string.

findings.title: No tax rate, service charge, currency, or receipt/printer configuration despite checkout now needing them
findings.evidence: Recent commits ('feat(web): checkout split payments + printable receipt') added tax computation and a printed receipt (bill.tax in checkout/-receipt-block.tsx), yet Settings — the only configuration surface in the app — has no field for tax rate, service charge %, currency, or which printer/receipt template to use.
findings.recommendation: Add a Billing/Receipt section to Settings once these values need to be venue-configurable rather than hardcoded/backend-only.

findings.title: Category edit/delete controls are hover-only — unreachable by touch
findings.evidence: Tablet screenshot (768x1024 logical / 1536x2048 capture): the 'Desserts' category row shows pencil and trash icons, but every sibling row (Starters, Pasta & Risotto, etc.) shows none — because the source wraps them in `hidden group-hover:flex` (apps/web/src/routes/_app/menu/index.tsx:918) with 24px `icon-xs` buttons. Same forced-hover row appears identically in the phone capture. There is no `:hover` state on a touchscreen, so on the app's primary device class a waiter/manager has no way at all to open the edit dialog or delete a category — the affordance literally never renders.
findings.recommendation: Make category row actions always-visible (as item cards already do), sized to at least 44x44px, e.g. reuse the ItemCard pattern of a persistent icon-button pair instead of group-hover reveal.

findings.title: The screen's one primary CTA uses the wrong token and fails the touch-target minimum
findings.evidence: Both screenshots show 'Add item' / 'New group' as the only filled button on the screen. It's rendered via the shared `<Button>` (no variant/size override, apps/web/src/routes/_app/menu/index.tsx:827,832), whose 'default' variant is `bg-primary text-primary-foreground` (button.tsx:11) and 'default' size is `h-8` (32px, button.tsx:23-24) — not the documented `bg-accent text-accent-foreground` CTA token, and 12px under the 44px touch minimum. It only reads as 'accent orange' because `--primary` and `--accent` happen to coincide in the default theme (apps/web/src/index.css:81,87); in monokai `--primary:#f8f8f2` vs `--accent:#fd971f` and in gruvbox `--primary:#ebdbb2` vs `--accent:#fe8019` — so in 2 of 4 themes this 'primary CTA' would render pale/cream instead of accent-colored.
findings.recommendation: Give the Add item/New group buttons an accent-token variant and size='lg' (or a dedicated touch-safe size), matching the documented CTA spec rather than the generic shadcn default.

findings.title: Item card edit/delete/availability controls are cramped, undersized, and visually identical at rest
findings.evidence: Tablet screenshot bottom row of each item card: the 'Available' pill, pencil (edit) and trash (delete) icons sit in one row with `gap-0.5` (2px) and `icon-sm` buttons (28px, button.tsx:31-32) — all well under the 44px target. Delete only turns red via `hover:text-destructive` (index.tsx:712), which never fires on touch, so at rest Edit and Delete are the same muted-gray icon separated by 2px of dead space next to a destructive action.
findings.recommendation: Increase hit area to >=44px, add a permanent (not hover-only) destructive tint to the delete icon, and add more horizontal separation or a divider before the delete control.

findings.title: Categories panel eats the entire first screen on tablet and phone before any item appears
findings.evidence: The Items-tab layout is `flex-col lg:flex-row` (index.tsx:870), so it only goes side-by-side at >=1024px CSS width. At the tablet capture (1536x2048 @2x = 768 CSS px, below `lg`) the Categories card (header + 6 rows + Add Category) fills essentially the whole viewport, leaving room for only ~2 rows of item cards (Bruschetta...Zuppa) with a 3rd row clipped — 6 of 20 items visible after already scrolling past the full category list. On the phone capture the same stack consumes the entire 780x1688 viewport and only 2 of 20 items are even partially visible.
findings.recommendation: Drop the split-layout breakpoint to `md` (768px) so tablet gets the two-pane view, and/or collapse categories into a horizontal scrollable chip row on narrower viewports instead of a tall vertical list.

findings.title: No station or modifier-group indicator on the item card
findings.evidence: The ItemSheet lets you assign a kitchen `station` (grill/cold/bar/pass, index.tsx:594-608) and attach modifier groups, but ItemCard (index.tsx:654-720) renders only name/price/description/available — nothing shows which station an item routes to or how many modifiers it has. A manager scanning the 20-item grid in the tablet screenshot can't verify KDS routing or modifier setup without opening every item individually.
findings.recommendation: Add a small station chip and modifier-count badge to the card footer, next to the Available pill.

findings.title: No search/filter on the item list
findings.evidence: Both screenshots show only a category filter (sidebar list with counts) and no search input, unlike the Inventory screen's 'Search items...' box seen in the same review set. At 20 items this is fine, but there's no way to find an item by name once the menu grows.
findings.recommendation: Add a search box above the item grid, consistent with the Inventory screen pattern already in the codebase.

findings.title: Category reordering requires typing a raw sort-order integer
findings.evidence: CategoryDialog (index.tsx:148-160) exposes a numeric 'Sort order' input as the only way to reorder categories — no drag handle or up/down control, on a touch-first app where dragging a category chip would be the natural interaction.
findings.recommendation: Replace with drag-to-reorder in the category list, or at minimum up/down arrow buttons.

findings.title: Can't create a modifier group from inside the item editor
findings.evidence: ItemSheet's modifier section (index.tsx:610-630) only lists and checks existing groups fetched via useMenuControllerGetModifierGroups — there's no inline 'New group' action, so adding an item that needs a not-yet-created modifier group forces the user to cancel, switch to the Modifiers tab, create it, then reopen the item sheet.
findings.recommendation: Add a small '+ New group' link inside the modifier picker that opens ModifierGroupSheet without leaving the item form.

perScreen.screenSummary: Visually the Menu screen is one of the more resolved screens in the revamp: warm cream canvas, a serif display heading, consistent card radii/shadows, strict semantic-token discipline (no raw hex or bg-white/zinc-* found in the file), thoughtful empty/loading states for every list, a confirm-before-delete guard, and a nicely authentic '86'd' label instead of a generic 'inactive' badge. The core weakness is that its touch-first mandate isn't actually honored at the interaction layer: category edit/delete affordances are hover-only and thus invisible on a tablet/phone, the screen's single CTA and every icon-button are sized well under the 44px minimum, and the categories-above-items stacked layout (triggered because the split only kicks in at `lg`/1024px) buries almost the entire item grid below the fold on both captured viewports. It reads as a competent, on-brand build that hasn't yet been touch-tested — the polish is real, but the primary interaction model for its stated audience (waiters/managers on tablets) is only partially wired up.
positives: Strict semantic-token discipline: bg-card/bg-background/border-border/text-muted-foreground/bg-success/bg-destructive used throughout, zero raw hex or bg-white/zinc-* found in the route file
Full loading-skeleton and empty-state coverage for categories, items, and modifier groups (not an afterthought)
Confirm-before-delete dialog guards both category and item deletion from accidental taps
Domain-authentic microcopy — '86'd' badge for unavailable items instead of a generic label
Category item-counts as pill badges and a consistent card grid give a clean, scannable structure
Structurally only one filled/primary-styled button appears per tab (Add item / New group), respecting the one-CTA rule at the component level even though its token is wrong
